source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which question gets the MOST thorough data about a client's recent sleep?
options: 'May we talk about your sleep lately?'
questions.rationale: An open question lets the client express thoughts and feelings. The others invite one-word answers, and one night is not a pattern.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q342 (PDF p. 510)
questions.quote: The remaining options could lead to a one-word answer that would not provide thorough assessment data.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY after arthroscopy?
questions.rationale: After arthroscopy, the priority is monitoring the affected area for numbness or tingling (neurovascular status).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q352 (PDF p. 520)
questions.quote: The priority nursing action is to monitor the affected area for numbness or tingling.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which discharge instruction fits a client after abdominal hysterectomy?
questions.rationale: After abdominal hysterectomy, the client avoids heavy lifting, limits stair climbing, and walks indoors at first, gradually increasing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q361 (PDF p. 529)
questions.quote: After abdominal hysterectomy, the client should avoid lifting anything that is heavy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drink should a client with a colostomy take regularly to help prevent odor?
questions.rationale: Parsley, yogurt, buttermilk, and cranberry juice help prevent colostomy odor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q398 (PDF p. 568)
questions.quote: Parsley, yogurt, buttermilk, and cranberry juice will prevent odor.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: While bathing a client, the nurse gets an emergency phone call. What should she do?
questions.rationale: For privacy and safety, the nurse covers the client and places the call light within reach before leaving.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q404 (PDF p. 577)
questions.quote: the nurse covers the client and places the call light within the client’s reach.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which reason for a restraint shows a need for MORE staff education?
options: Immobilize a limb for a procedure
Keep the client in bed at night
questions.rationale: Restraints limit movement when a limb must be immobilized. They are not used to keep a client in bed at night or as punishment or convenience.
explanations: Correct answer: not a valid reason.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q405 (PDF p. 579)
questions.quote: Restraints are not applied to keep a client in bed at night

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding in an older client calls for a fall-prevention protocol?
questions.rationale: Aging changes such as limited range of motion, decreased peripheral vision, and slowed nerve conduction increase accident risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q407 (PDF p. 581)
questions.quote: The physiological changes that occur during the aging process increase the client’s risk for accidents.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which measure prevents intestinal parasite spread in a preschool?
options: Keep sick children at home only
questions.rationale: Intestinal parasites spread by the fecal-oral route; standard precautions with handwashing prevent transmission.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q411 (PDF p. 587)
questions.quote: The fecal-oral route is the mode of transmission of an intestinal parasitical disease.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should the nurse do when moving a client from the OR table to a stretcher?
options: Check LOC and tell the client
questions.rationale: For safe transfer the nurse assesses LOC, tells the client about the transfer, and ensures enough help and locked wheels.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q416 (PDF p. 593)
questions.quote: the nurse should assess the client’s level of consciousness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After bronchoscopy with sedation and topical anesthetic, what is the PRIORITY?
options: Give water to soothe the throat
Keep NPO until gag reflex returns
questions.rationale: The client stays NPO until cough, gag, and swallow reflexes return (usually 1–2 hours), then starts with ice chips.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q433 (PDF p. 611)
questions.quote: the client remains NPO until the cough, gag, and swallow reflexes have returned

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A home care client recovering from a mild stroke lives alone. Which assessment checks safety risk?
questions.rationale: Safety assessment includes visual acuity, gait and posture, and muscle strength because changes raise fall risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q438 (PDF p. 617)
questions.quote: The assessment should include assessing visual acuity, gait and posture, and muscle strength

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a MEDICAL asepsis (clean technique) action?
questions.rationale: Medical asepsis reduces and prevents the spread of microorganisms through hand hygiene, cleaning the environment, and clean gloves.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q439 (PDF p. 619)
questions.quote: Medical asepsis, or clean technique, includes procedures to reduce and prevent the spread of microorganisms.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a radial ABG draw, how is bleeding prevented?
questions.rationale: Pressure over the site for 5 to 10 minutes prevents hematoma and arterial damage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q441 (PDF p. 621)
questions.quote: Applying pressure over the puncture site for 5 to 10 minutes reduces the risk of hematoma formation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is an AV fistula arm BEST protected on admission?
options: Put an allergy band on it
Place an alert band: no BP or IV
questions.rationale: No venipunctures or BP on the access arm; an alert bracelet communicates this to all caregivers.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q442 (PDF p. 622)
questions.quote: There should be no venipunctures or blood pressure measurements in the extremity with a hemodialysis access device.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which finding is a NEGATIVE outcome of wrist restraints?
questions.rationale: Negative outcomes include impaired skin, poor circulation, agitation, and incontinence.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q465 (PDF p. 647)
questions.quote: Negative outcomes in the use of restraints include signs of impaired skin in

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does the nurse reduce infection risk in a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: Concentrated glucose supports bacterial growth, so aseptic technique for dressing, tubing, and bag changes reduces infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q467 (PDF p. 651)
questions.quote: the concentrated glucose solutions are an excellent medium for bacterial growth.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client gets dizzy sitting up for thoracentesis. Which alternate position is safest?
questions.rationale: If the client cannot sit, he lies on the unaffected side with the head elevated so fluid collects on the affected side.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q504 (PDF p. 699)
questions.quote: Positioning can help isolate the fluid in a pleural effusion

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which finding shows a restraint was applied UNSAFELY?
questions.rationale: A restraint is never applied snugly because it impairs circulation. Slip knots and a reachable call bell are correct.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q512 (PDF p. 707)
questions.quote: A restraint should never be applied snugly because it could impair circulation.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is a safety guideline for physical restraints?
questions.rationale: Restraints need a prescription, are secured to the bed frame with a quick-release knot, and are checked often.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q570 (PDF p. 775)
questions.quote: A physical restraint is a mechanical or physical device that is used to immobilize a client or extremity.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food is allowed on a low-bacteria (neutropenic) diet?
questions.rationale: Low-bacteria diets allow cooked foods such as bread, baked chicken, and well-done meat; raw produce and undercooked eggs are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q514 (PDF p. 709)
questions.quote: In the immunocompromised client, a low-bacteria diet is implemented.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A post-op client has episodes of extreme agitation. What prevents escalation?
questions.rationale: Slow speech and movement prevent escalation; sudden moves may trigger violence. Touch may be misread.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q516 (PDF p. 711)
questions.quote: Speaking and moving slowly toward the client will prevent the client from becoming further agitated

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse drops a used syringe on the floor. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Used syringes go into a sharps container immediately. Sweeping risks needlesticks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q518 (PDF p. 713)
questions.quote: Used syringes should always be placed in a sharps container immediately after use

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with partial left leg hemiplegia needs more support than a straight cane. Which device fits?
questions.rationale: A tripod or quad cane gives multiple points of support for partial or complete hemiplegia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q523 (PDF p. 719)
questions.quote: A tripod or quadripod cane may be prescribed for the client who requires greater support and stability

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the INITIAL action when a post-op client sits up to prepare for walking?
questions.rationale: Ambulation should not exceed tolerance, so the client is assessed for dizziness and hypotension first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q526 (PDF p. 723)
questions.quote: The client should be assessed for dizziness and hypotension before ambulation begins.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which action prevents electrical shock with equipment?
questions.rationale: Use grounded three-prong plugs, check cords for fraying, and keep cords away from water.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q527 (PDF p. 725)
questions.quote: checking the electrical cord for fraying or other dam

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a home IV pump be used safely?
questions.rationale: Equipment needs grounding; extension cords are never recommended, so the client sits near a three-prong outlet.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q579 (PDF p. 784)
questions.quote: Extension cords are never recommended

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is a client moved from stretcher to bed after spinal fusion?
questions.rationale: A transfer board and four people give optimal stabilization of the spine.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q528 (PDF p. 726)
questions.quote: the client is transferred from the stretcher to the bed using a transfer board and the assistance of four people.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Besides handwashing, what should the nurse do before entering the room of a client with active TB?
questions.rationale: TB is airborne, so the nurse wears a particulate (HEPA/N95) respirator; hands are washed before and after care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q533 (PDF p. 731)
questions.quote: The nurse wears a HEPA respirator when caring for a client with active tuberculosis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which equipment should be at the bedside for a pleural biopsy?
questions.rationale: Complications include hemothorax and pneumothorax, so a chest tube and drainage system are kept ready.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q535 (PDF p. 733)
questions.quote: Complications after pleural biopsy include hemothorax, pneumothorax

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During hemodialysis, which action by a new nurse needs correction?
questions.rationale: The connection site should stay visible to check for bleeding, ischemia, and infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q536 (PDF p. 734)
questions.quote: the connection site should not be covered, and it should be visible

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse and a dialysis client are drinking coffee during treatment. What should the manager do?
questions.rationale: Dialysis-associated hepatitis B is a risk, so no eating or drinking in the client area.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q560 (PDF p. 761)
questions.quote: A potential complication of hemodialysis is the acquisition of dialysis-associated hepatitis B.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What must be in place before a MUGA scan?
questions.rationale: A radioisotope is injected IV for the MUGA scan, so signed informed consent is needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q539 (PDF p. 737)
questions.quote: A radioisotope is injected intravenously. Therefore, a signed informed consent is

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nursing attendant asks how to protect herself caring for a client with chlamydial urethritis. What does the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Chlamydia is sexually transmitted; caregivers cannot catch it through care, so standard precautions suffice.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q544 (PDF p. 744)
questions.quote: Caregivers cannot acquire the disease during administration of care

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before bronchoscopy?
questions.rationale: Bronchoscopy is invasive and requires informed consent. The client is NPO beforehand.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q554 (PDF p. 755)
questions.quote: Because the procedure is invasive, it requires obtaining informed consent

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A hospitalized child exposed to varicella 2 weeks ago develops a trunk rash. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Varicella incubation is 14–21 days; the child is isolated at once to prevent spread.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q559 (PDF p. 760)
questions.quote: The incubation period is 14 to 21 days.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should the client know about shock wave lithotripsy?
options: The stone passes as fine sand in urine
questions.rationale: Lithotripsy is noninvasive; shock waves shatter the stone into fine sand passed in the urine.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q565 (PDF p. 768)
questions.quote: The stone is broken into fine sand, which is passed in the client

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older client is 4 days post-ORIF for hip fracture. Which measure keeps her safe?
options: Ask her to call before getting up
questions.rationale: Age, surgery, and opioids raise fall risk, so she calls for help before getting up.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q572 (PDF p. 777)
questions.quote: The nurse instructs the client to call for help before getting up

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which home oxygen safety teaching is correct?
options: Hold the tank on your lap in the car
questions.rationale: Check the oxygen level often so it does not run out. Tanks are secured when traveling and kept away from heat and flames.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q578 (PDF p. 783)
questions.quote: The nurse instructs the client and family to check the oxygen level in the tank on a regular basis
